body.claim: Within range, only one transmitter can transmit on a Wi-Fi channel at a time.
body.why: Wi-Fi radio bands are divided into channels, and channels can be shared between networks. With CSMA/CA, devices begin transmitting only after sensing the channel is idle. Two stations may sense it idle at the same time, so collisions cannot be completely prevented.

probes.question: How do Wi-Fi devices share a channel?
options: They start transmitting only after sensing the channel is idle

probes.question: True or false: CSMA/CA completely prevents collisions.

sources.title: Carrier-sense multiple access with collision avoidance (Wikipedia)

claims.claim: Within range, only one transmitter can transmit on a channel at a time; channels can be shared between networks
claims.quote: Channels can be shared between networks, but, within range, only one transmitter can transmit on a channel at a time.

claims.claim: Wi-Fi radio bands are divided into channels
claims.quote: these bands are subdivided into multiple channels

claims.claim: CSMA/CA: devices begin transmitting only after sensing the channel idle (probe 1)
claims.quote: With CSMA/CA, stations attempt to avoid collisions by beginning transmission only after the channel is sensed to be idle

claims.claim: Two stations may sense idle simultaneously so collisions are not completely prevented (probe 2: false)
claims.quote: CSMA/CA cannot completely prevent collisions, as two stations may sense the channel to be idle at the same time
